text:
maria: quick note — during a morning perf sweep i saw a pattern where long-sequence tenant requests were piling up behind many short requests after kv-cache misses. overall throughput looked fine but p95 for the long requests spiked ~3x

hao: can you paste the experiment config + queue metrics? curious if this is an obvious batching shape issue or a token-budget policy bug

maria: pasting snippet from the test cluster (small redwood-dedicated pool):

```json
{
  "batcher": {
    "max_batch_token_budget": 2048,
    "min_batch_tokens": 8,
    "queue_policy": "size_then_age",
    "age_threshold_ms": 60
  },
  "kv_cache": {
    "enabled": true,
    "prefetch_seconds": 0.5
  }
}
```

maria: metrics: long-req median latency ~120ms, p95 ~560ms during traffic spike; short reqs median ~40ms. KV miss rate bumped from 6% -> 22% in the same window

rachel: interesting. sounds like when cache misses happen we rehydrate kv and that increases per-request token work, but the batcher keeps packing short requests which inflates combined sequence length and delays the long ones?

hao: yep. when the batcher picks by queue depth without accounting for estimated token work it can create large mixed batches that saturate the sequence-level budget. the long request ends up waiting for the batch to flush.

kyle: what's our current token accounting flow? we charge by tokens when a batch is formed or when it's dispatched? small detail but affects ordering incentives

maria: token budget is computed on batch formation: we sum expected tokens per request (based on early metadata) and compare to max_batch_token_budget. but we only update per-tenant token debt after dispatch. so a tenant with many short requests can repeatedly join batches before the long tenant's single request is scheduled

rachel: thought — try smoothing the per-tenant token target with an exponential moving average so a burst of shorts doesn't instantly consume the tenant's share. i tried a quick experiment: smoothing_alpha=0.3 and a tiny fairness multiplier for long sequences

rachel: config snippet i used:

```yaml
batcher:
  max_batch_token_budget: 2048
  per_tenant_target_tokens_ema_alpha: 0.3
  per_seq_length_penalty: true
  short_seq_bonus_tokens: 4
```

rachel: result: p95 for long-req dropped from 560ms -> 240ms, short req median increased ~6ms but p50 stayed stable

hao: nice. what's the steady-state throughput impact? any regressions on overall tokens/s?

rachel: minimal. tokens/s down ~1.8% in the window. kv miss tail still a factor though — we saw fewer large mixed batches because tenant weights stopped shifting as fast

perf-bot: profiling summary attached: top kernel time increased on matmul-ffn by 12% during the miss storms. kv rehydration adds ~30-80 tokens extra on misses depending on prefix length

maria: thanks perf-bot. so two levers: 1) per-tenant smoothing + per-sequence adjustments; 2) proactively delaying short requests if they would create a mixed batch that penalizes an existing long request in the queue

kyle: gating shorts feels risky for PLG UX but if we only apply when queue imbalance > threshold and prioritize long sequences hitting SLOs maybe ok. we need safety: max-block ms, and a fallback to oldest-first after Xms

hao: another idea: during kv miss windows mark requests with a 'rehydration-estimate' flag and prefer to form homogeneous batches (same rehydration profile) to avoid variability in kernel selection and execution time

maria: homogenous batching for kv-miss vs kv-hit is neat. might simplify kernel selection too (less kernel switching per batch). would need quick estimate phase though

rachel: i can run a focused A/B on canary: implement ema smoothing + homogeneous batching for kv-marked requests. measure p95 for long-seq tenants, short-seq latency, and tokens/s. i'll bake in guarded feature flag

maria: can you include a trace hook so we can attribute latency to (batch_wait | kv_rehydrate | compute_kernel)

rachel: yes — add `trace.stage` tags. sample traces at 1% and full histograms for canary nodes

infra-bot: deploy request queued: canary-batcher-alloc-smoothing -> infra/canaries (owner=rachel)

hao: add test to ensure oldest-first fallback after 200ms so we don't deadlock a long request behind repeated short bursts

rachel: added. also adding a soft limit: if tenant_ema_tokens > 0.8*max_batch_token_budget then deprioritize that tenant until debt decreases

maria: action items: rachel run canary + share perf delta + traces, hao add oldest-first fallback test, kyle review UX risk and SLO gating, i'll iterate on policy thresholds after initial results

kyle: acked. please post canary link in this thread when ready

maria: thanks team, will follow up tomorrow with numbers
